title: karpathy/nanochat: a small harness for training a chat model on one GPU node
friendlyTitle: karpathy/nanochat: a small toolkit for training a chat model on one GPU machine
summary: nanochat is Andrej Karpathy's experimental stack for training a language model on one GPU node, from tokenizer through pretraining, fine-tuning, evaluation, and a simple chat. The speedrun script targets GPT-2 grade on an 8xH100 node. The README's cost example is about $48 for two hours, at about $24 an hour for that node, and closer to $15 on a spot instance. The leaderboard's latest listed row is 1.65 hours, dated 14 March 2026. The default branch last changed on 3 July 2026. MIT. GitHub's Python trending list showed 551 stars today, and about 60,200 in total.
friendlySummary: nanochat is Andrej Karpathy's experimental toolkit for training a language model on one GPU machine. It covers the tokenizer, pretraining, fine-tuning, evaluation, and a simple chat. The speedrun script aims for GPT-2 level on a machine with eight H100 chips. The README's cost example is about $48 for two hours, at about $24 an hour for that machine, and closer to $15 on a cheaper spot rental. The leaderboard's latest listed row is 1.65 hours, dated 14 March 2026. The main branch last changed on 3 July 2026. The license is MIT. GitHub's Python trending list showed 551 stars today, and about 60,200 in total.
whyItMatters: Use it to see the whole training loop in one readable repo, or to run the published speedrun if you already have an 8xH100 node. It is not a chatbot you install on a laptop and call ChatGPT. The $48 figure is the README's example for about two hours, not a quote for the 1.65-hour leaderboard row.
